title: Set up Docker or Podman on a machine
goal: A working container runtime that passes a hello-world run

version.change_notes: First Shippin version: Docker Desktop (Windows WSL 2, macOS), Engine rootless/rootful and Podman on Linux.

steps.title: What we are about to set up
steps.text: A container runtime runs apps in isolated containers. On macOS and Windows it runs inside a small Linux VM; on Linux it runs directly. I will only run the runtime and its installer, and you do every step that needs admin rights.

steps.title: Pick the path for this operating system
Choose a runtime
steps.question: Which runtime do you want? Rootless Docker Engine is the default because it avoids root-level access.

steps.title: Choose a runtime
steps.question: Docker Desktop is the default on macOS; Podman is the alternative.

steps.title: Choose a runtime
steps.question: Docker Desktop on the WSL 2 backend is the default on Windows; Podman is the alternative.

steps.title: Docker Desktop licence
steps.question: Is this for personal use, education, or an organisation with at most 250 employees and at most $10 million revenue? Larger organisations need a paid Docker subscription.

steps.title: Switch to Podman
steps.question: Podman has no licence step. Continue with Podman?

steps.title: Ask for setup access
steps.reason: To check for and verify the container runtime, I need to run only docker/podman and their installers and reach the vendor download hosts until this setup task ends.
steps.changes: A task-length grant on this machine

steps.title: Pick the check for the chosen runtime
Install Podman with your package manager

text_by_os.linux: Open a terminal and run this command. It needs sudo, so you run it, not me.

text_by_os.macos: Open Terminal and run this command (Homebrew), or install Podman Desktop from podman.io.

text_by_os.windows: Open PowerShell and run this command, then reopen PowerShell.

steps.title: Create the Podman machine
steps.changes: Creates a small Linux VM for Podman

steps.title: Optional: point Docker tools at Podman

text_by_os.macos: If you use Docker tools, set DOCKER_HOST to the socket podman machine start printed. Skip this otherwise.
text_by_os.windows: If you use Docker tools, set DOCKER_HOST to the pipe podman machine start printed. Skip this otherwise.

steps.changes: Your shell configuration, if you choose

steps.title: Install rootless prerequisites

text_by_os.linux: Run this with sudo in your own terminal. Rootless mode needs uidmap and at least 65,536 subordinate UIDs and GIDs for your user.

steps.changes: Installs uidmap and the rootless extras

steps.title: Set up the rootless daemon for your user
Install Docker Engine from Docker's repository

text_by_os.linux: Run these commands with sudo in your own terminal.

steps.changes: Adds Docker's apt repository and installs Engine

steps.title: Optional: add yourself to the docker group

text_by_os.linux: Skip this unless you need docker without sudo. Run: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER, then log out and in.

steps.changes: Your user gains root-level privileges via Docker

steps.title: Published ports and your firewall
steps.text: Ports published by Docker Engine bypass ufw and firewalld rules. Publish ports on 127.0.0.1 (for example -p 127.0.0.1:8080:80) unless you mean to expose them.

steps.title: Install Docker Desktop

text_by_os.macos: Download Docker Desktop for your chip from docker.com, open Docker.dmg, drag Docker to Applications, start it and approve the privileged helper prompt.

steps.changes: Installs Docker Desktop and its helper
steps.check: The whale icon shows Docker is running

steps.title: Install WSL 2

text_by_os.windows: Open PowerShell as administrator, run this command, then restart Windows.

steps.changes: Installs WSL and a Linux kernel; needs a restart

steps.title: Install Docker Desktop (per-user)

text_by_os.windows: Run the Docker Desktop installer and choose the per-user install with the WSL 2 backend. Accept its terms yourself.

steps.changes: Installs Docker Desktop for your user

steps.title: Accept Docker's agreement yourself
steps.question: Docker Desktop shows its subscription agreement on first start. Have you read and accepted it? I will not click Accept for you.

steps.title: What was installed and how to undo it
steps.text: The runtime is installed and verified. Stop it from its menu or with podman machine stop. Uninstall with your package manager or the app's uninstaller. The setup access ends with this task.
